newsitem.title: UK: EMU seen as positive or neutral for credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: EMU seen as positive or neutral for credit ratings.

text.p: European rating agency IBCA said on Thursday that European Economic and Monetary (EMU) would be positive or neutral for the sovereign credit ratings of participating countries.
But IBCA said that governments involved in EMU would not automatically be rated AAA.
Although members of the currency union would have the power to tax in the euro common currency, they would lose their power to print money and would therefore not necessarily be rated AAA.

"The ratings will therefore be more like the foreign currency rating of the likely participants -- AA plus for Belgium and Ireland and AA for Finland -- than their local currency ratings -- AAA in the case of all likely participants," IBCA said in a report.

The rating agency said that although small, peripheral European countries -- such as Finland and Ireland -- were more vulnerable to economic shocks, they also had more flexible labour markets, meaning that the loss of the exchange rate as a means of monetary adjustment was less serious.

"Given the other benefits -- notably substantial savings in foreign exchange transaction costs which are proportionately higher for small countries, and a likely investment increase -- the rating implications would be positive or neutral," IBCA said.
